title: Read-only live board by default
description: Objective: the control room's default view is the real daemon, not fixtures. Measured at HEAD 1aa7cdc: main.tsx:38-41 gates live mode behind ?live=1 with the doc comment 'DEVELOPMENT-ONLY live attachment'; default mounts ControlRoomScaffold over 245 lines of frozen fixtures (fixtures.ts, CONTROL_ROOM_FIXTURE_KIND = DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY). Live mode already works: polls /command,/events/read,/events/ack,/affordances/read,/documents/dossier/read via the Vite proxy (vite.config.ts:58-67, MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN default 127.0.0.1:39123), refuses closed without VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL + VITE_MOE_LIVE_CSRF (live-config.ts:51-58). The daemon needs ZERO changes — it already serves every read the board uses. Deliverable: invert the gate — live is the default when credentials are configured, fixtures only behind an explicit ?fixtures=1 (labeled as fixture in the UI); strip drag-to-dispatch from the default board (live-board.tsx:154-199 draggable READY cards + live-dispatch.ts) keeping ONLY the credentialed approval dispatch (human decision: command-chain surface, approvals stay); document the serving story (vite dev/preview + proxy) in the runbook. Scope: apps/control-room only. Update affected tests (live-board.test.tsx, live-board.a11y.test.tsx, live-app tests). Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck && test (nonzero count line), pnpm typecheck, plus manual smoke against a scratch daemon.
definitionOfDone: Default mount with credentials configured is the live board; absent credentials renders a clear configuration notice (not fixtures); fixtures render only behind ?fixtures=1 with a visible fixture label - all three arms asserted in tests.
Drag-to-dispatch is removed from the board; approval decide remains behind the session credential; a test asserts no dispatch path exists for non-approval commands from the UI.
Daemon sources untouched; only apps/control-room files change; runbook documents the serving story.
pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck and test exit 0 with a nonzero Test Files count line; pnpm typecheck exits 0; only explicit owned paths committed.
taskRails: Daemon unchanged; this task is apps/control-room + docs only.
Fail closed: no credential means a configuration notice, never silent fixture fallback presented as live data.
Keep the truth-chip / UNKNOWN rendering invariants the existing browser journeys pin (tests/e2e/control-room).

implementationPlan.description: TDD the gate inversion as a TRI-STATE resolver, pure and testable apart from React. Today main.tsx:39-40 mounts LiveControlRoom only on ?live=1, scaffold otherwise. RED tests (new resolver test file beside main, or extend the live-app test surface) for a resolveShellMode(search, buildSetup) function returning exactly one of: (a) LIVE — build credentials present (resolveLiveSetupFromBuild() yields a config; live-config.ts:51-58 already refuses closed without VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL + VITE_MOE_LIVE_CSRF) and ?fixtures=1 absent; (b) FIXTURES — ?fixtures=1 explicitly present, regardless of credentials; (c) CONFIG_NOTICE — credentials absent and fixtures not requested: a notice NAMING both missing env variables (assert the two exact names in the rendered output), never a silent fixture fallback presented as data. Also pin: the legacy ?live=1 param still resolves LIVE when credentials exist (old links keep working) and resolves CONFIG_NOTICE, not a crash, without them. TOPOLOGY DECISION (comment-1d163d7b, binding): dev-proxy topology — do not touch the daemon, do not weaken origin guards.
implementationPlan.note:
TRI-STATE RESOLVER landed, TDD. RED first: `npx vitest run src/shell-mode.test.ts` -> "Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests" (module absent). GREEN after: "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 11 passed (11)".

SHAPE. `resolveShellMode(search: string, setup: LiveSetupResult): ShellMode` in a new pure module `src/shell-mode.ts` (60 lines). Returns exactly one of SHELL_MODES = ["CONFIG_NOTICE","FIXTURES","LIVE"]. No React, no import.meta.env read - the build's setup is PASSED IN, which is what makes every arm assertable by value.

THE TWO REFUSAL ARMS ARE PRODUCTION'S, NOT MINE. The test builds them by calling `resolveLiveSetup({}, null)` and `resolveLiveSetup({VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL:"cred",VITE_MOE_LIVE_CSRF:"csrf"}, null)` and asserts their codes are LIVE_CONFIG_MISSING and LIVE_COMPAT_REFUSED respectively. A hand-written `{ok:false,code:"LIVE_CONFIG_MISSING"}` would have stayed green the day live-config stopped minting that code; this cannot. Only the ADMITTED arm is a literal, because the gate that mints a real one needs GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS and the barrel exports only its TYPE - the resolver reads nothing but `.ok` on that arm.

DISCRIMINATION DECISION, and it is the non-obvious one. CONFIG_NOTICE is keyed to the code LIVE_CONFIG_MISSING, NOT to `!setup.ok`. A compat refusal means credentials WERE configured and the gate refused - printing "set VITE_MOE_LIVE_CREDENTIAL" there would name the wrong cause. So LIVE_COMPAT_REFUSED resolves LIVE and the live attachment renders its own stable code through the existing LiveRefusedPanel. Pinned by its own test.

PRECEDENCE, pinned: `?fixtures=1` wins over a legacy `?live=1` in the same URL (both directions of the parameter order asserted). Reason recorded in the module doc: the fixture request is the only one honourable regardless of what the build carries, so its meaning never depends on who built the bundle.

FAIL-CLOSED, pinned: absent credentials + no fixture request -> CONFIG_NOTICE, never FIXTURES. Also pinned that `?fixtures=0`, `?fixtures=`, `?fixtures` and `?fixtures=true` are NOT fixture requests (a stale `?fixtures=0` link must not serve frozen fixtures over a credentialed build) - a truthiness test would have admitted all four.

LEGACY: `?live=1` still resolves LIVE with credentials and CONFIG_NOTICE without them - old links keep working, and without credentials they refuse rather than crash.

Topology per binding comment-1d163d7b honoured: zero daemon files touched, no origin guard read or weakened.

implementationPlan.description: Strip mutation dispatch from the live board, keeping ONLY approval decide. Today live-board.tsx:154-199 wires draggable READY cards through live-dispatch.ts (279 lines). RED first in live-board.test.tsx: (a) no card is draggable regardless of status; (b) no dispatch affordance exists for any non-approval command kind — assert by the ABSENCE of the dispatch handler/affordance on rendered non-approval cards AND by asserting the only command kind the board can emit is approval.decide (inspect the dispatch surface the component exposes, not just the DOM); (c) the approval path still dispatches with the session credential exactly as before (existing tests keep passing). Then implement: remove drag wiring from live-board.tsx; live-dispatch.ts shrinks to the approval payload path (do NOT delete the module — the seed script task references its payloadFor shapes as documentation; leave non-approval builders exported but unreachable from the UI, or move them under a clearly-named export the board no longer imports — state the choice in the step note).
implementationPlan.note:
BOARD IS READ-ONLY EXCEPT approval.decide. Package suite after: "Test Files 73 passed (73) / Tests 904 passed (904)" (was 72/885). tsc exit 0. live-board.tsx 202 lines / 7505 bytes.

TDD: new src/live/live-board-readonly.test.tsx RED first - "Tests 17 failed | 2 passed (19)" - then 19 passed.

DECISION ON live-dispatch.ts, and it is NOT the one the step offered by default. I left the module UNCHANGED - no shrink, no guard. Reason, measured not assumed: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:191 dynamically imports `../../../control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts` and calls `payloadFor(kind, target)` for ARBITRARY kinds (:234). Deleting or narrowing the non-approval payloads would break a daemon file this task's rail forbids me to touch. So the step's sanctioned alternative applies: "leave non-approval builders exported but unreachable from the UI". They are exported, the daemon still uses them, and the BOARD reaches none of them.

I also deliberately did NOT add a kind guard inside dispatchAffordance. The board calls it from exactly one place, behind the render guard, so that branch would be unreachable from any honest fixture - a dead guard that no drill can flip, which is its own defect. The restriction lives where DoD 2 puts it: the UI.

THE RULE, one exported function. `boardMayDispatch(step)` = status READY && kind === BOARD_DISPATCH_COMMAND_KIND ("approval.decide"). live-board.tsx renders its control through that exact call, and `dispatch` is invoked from that control's onClick and nowhere else.

REMOVED: draggable + onDragStart on cards, onDragOver/onDrop on all three columns, onDropCommitted, refuseDrop, DRAG_STEP_IDENTITY, the dropNote state and its paragraph, and the `DragEvent` type import. Also the two CSS rules that ADVERTISED the gone gesture: `.cr-liveboard-card[draggable="true"]{cursor:grab}` and the dropnote block - leaving `cursor: grab` behind would have kept promising a gesture that no longer exists.

ASSERTIONS (19), two independent axes so neither can go vacuous alone:
- PREDICATE SWEEP over `Object.keys(DEV_PAYLOADS)` read from production (12 kinds), each asserting `boardMayDispatch(...) === (kind === approval.decide)`. Guarded by a corpus test: roster non-empty, contains the approval kind, and contains >4 others - a sweep over an emptied roster generates zero cases and passes green.
- DOM: over that same all-kinds READY surface, every kind paints a card (count asserted = roster length, so the absence of controls is about controls and not about missing cards) and `[data-testid^='cr.liveboard.dispatch.']` equals EXACTLY the approval id; `container.querySelectorAll("button")` length 1.
- NO DRAG: zero `[draggable]` attributes at all (not just zero ="true"), and dragStart+drop onto Committed sends NOTHING - asserted on the transport, not on the DOM.
- TRANSPORT: click EVERY button the board rendered, then assert the set of `commandKind` values that reached sendCommand is exactly ["approval.decide"].
- APPROVAL PATH INTACT: daemon-minted commandId and expectedVersion pass through untouched AND `sessionCredential` on the envelope is the session's value, not a literal.
- READY is load-bearing: BLOCKED and COMMITTED approval cards are refused too.

THREE EXISTING SUITES UPDATED, each because the board genuinely changed.
1. live-board.test.tsx: dispatch fixtures moved project.register -> approval.decide (a fixture on any other kind now asserts over a control that does not exist). The drag test kept its CLAIM - with two same-kind cards, the control used must dispatch that card's affordance and not its neighbour's - and is now driven by the target-specific accessible name, the only thing that still distinguishes two controls sharing a data-testid.
2. live-board.a11y.test.tsx: same kind swap; its repeated-kind accessible-name and live-region pins are unchanged and still green.
3. live-effort-path.test.tsx: SPLIT INTO TWO DRIVERS. `dispatchThroughBoard` still renders LiveControlRoom and clicks the real button - kept for the APPROVE arms, so the click-to-seam edge stays proven - and it asserts its argument IS the approval kind rather than timing out on a missing control. `dispatchThroughSeam` calls `dispatchAffordance` directly, the same production function that click handler calls, with byte-identical affordance records to what surfaceBody puts on the wire. Every assertion in that file survived unchanged: all four decision kinds, the exact cardinality of 4, ADDITIONAL derivation, FREE_INTERACTION, ATTENTION_SWITCH (now crossing drivers, which proves the surface identity comes from the seam and not from a DOM element), and both refusal arms with their exact code AND layer. Only one assertion changed FORM: the CREATE arm read "EFFECTS_COMMITTED" off the rendered card and now reads it off the returned DispatchReport - same production answer, different reader.

A11Y. live-board.a11y.test.tsx keeps every existing pin green unchanged (target-specific accessible names on repeated kinds, role=status/aria-live=polite on the async report and the refusal surface). Added one test that asserts the removal did not cost anything: zero `[draggable]` attributes AND the surviving control is still keyboard-reachable - no positive tabindex, and one Tab press lands on it. RUNBOOK. New "## Control room (serving story)" section - the exact heading the CONFIG_NOTICE arm points an operator at, so the notice's reference resolves. Two things documented there that are non-obvious and would otherwise bite:

- the Origin rewrite in vite.config.ts is LOAD-BEARING: the daemon refuses a non-loopback Origin with LISTENER_ORIGIN_INVALID, so serving the built bundle from an unrecognised origin - or opening dist/index.html off the filesystem - fails closed. Stated as the v0.1 topology with production-honest serving explicitly deferred to v0.2.
